title: Sparkling Water 12-pack

drivers.name: Halloween (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect from 2 past occurrences: x0.93 vs baseline; 2025: x0.57, 2024: x0.84, 2023: x0.7 (with promotion).

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: No direct data, but new competitors typically reduce demand in nearby stores; plausible downside given local competition shift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 95.3. Halloween (event week) has historically lowered demand: noise-adjusted effect is x0.93, based on two past occurrences. The competitor opening across the street adds downward pressure, though no direct evidence of impact exists. The price is unchanged (no discount), so no uplift. The classical model's x0.93 is a reasonable start but underweights the competitor risk. We adjust down slightly more, to x0.89, with moderate downside spread to reflect uncertainty in the competitor's impact. The historical noise-adjusted effect is already shrunk, so no further shrinkage needed.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 95.3 | 5%-95%: 26.7 - 185.6 | 10%-90%: 59.9 - 153.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-39% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
